answer_raw:
Claude’s newest overall model is **Sonnet 5.5** (the top‑tier version released in late‑June 2026; the baseline line is Sonnet 4.5). It is billed as the best for agents, coding, and computer use, and it delivers exceptional coding performance across the entire software development lifecycle. It costs **$2 / 1 M input tokens** and **$10 / 1 M output tokens**, with up to **90 % savings** when you cache prompts and **50 %** when you batch requests, and you can only access it through the Claude API【1】.

The most recent ChatGPT variant is **GPT‑5.6 Sol** (released July 2026). In the latest public benchmark, it scores **59 on the Intelligence Index**, a close second to Claude Fable 5’s 60, and it is **#1 on the Coding Agent Index**. A notable feature of GPT-5.6 is that requests exceeding **272K input tokens** reprice the entire request at **2× input / 1.5× output**, which can affect large-scale coding tasks.

### Coding choice

Both models excel at code generation, but the evidence points to **GPT‑5.6 Sol as the clear leader for frontier coding performance** (top coding‑agent ranking). **Sonnet 5.5 is cheaper and offers strong savings when you cache or batch prompts, and it’s straightforward to integrate via the Claude API**.

- If **budget or API simplicity** is your priority, choose **Sonnet 5.5**.
If you prioritize cutting-edge coding performance and can manage the cost and variable pricing, GPT-5.6 Sol may be the better choice.
